requirements.title: System Layout and CAD
requirements.definition: Provide the mechanical system layout and CAD/design drawings needed to define the prototype's component placement and enclosure.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the layout and CAD artifact only; the BOM, wiring plan, and physical product behaviors remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Component Bill of Materials
requirements.definition: Provide and refine a bill of materials identifying compatible components for constructing the prototype.
requirements.boundary_note: The BOM is an independently requested executable artifact; individual product behaviors implemented by its components are not attributes of this Requirement.

requirements.title: Electrical Wiring Plan
requirements.definition: Provide a basic electrical wiring plan or overview for the prototype's motors, controls, valves, fans, and power system.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the wiring documentation artifact rather than the operational capacity or safety of the implemented electrical system.

requirements.title: Operational Prototype Demonstration
requirements.definition: Provide a clear operational demonstration showing the prototype's specified mixing, speed-control, dispensing, continuous-operation, and leak-free behaviors.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a standalone acceptance artifact repeatedly requested before shipment, not a generic testing or debugging Requirement.

requirements.title: Dual Independent Mixing Stations
requirements.definition: The machine must provide two independently controllable mixing stations that can operate simultaneously.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers station count and independent/simultaneous operation; speed range, whisk performance, and dispensing are separately testable behaviors.

requirements.title: Matcha Mixing and Frothing Performance
requirements.definition: Each station must use a suitable whisk configuration and position to mix fine matcha powder smoothly and produce consistent aeration and foam.
requirements.boundary_note: Whisk style, material, diameter, depth, and adapter are attributes of one mixing-head mechanism; motor speed control and splash containment can change independently.

requirements.title: Independent Variable-Speed Drive
requirements.definition: Each mixer must have independently adjustable motor speed supporting low-speed mixing and higher-speed frothing while preserving usable torque.
requirements.boundary_note: Motor maximum RPM, usable adjustment range, torque, and knob limiting are attributes of the speed-control mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Splash and Mess Control
requirements.definition: The prototype must limit splashing and mess during mixing across its intended speed range through positioning, bowl geometry, speed tuning, or a guard.
requirements.boundary_note: Splash containment has its own acceptance outcome and can fail independently of whether the drink is adequately mixed.

requirements.title: Mixing Bowl Size and Geometry
requirements.definition: Use relatively small, deep bowls whose capacity and proportions support mixing quality, foam consistency, visual event cycles, and the intended enclosure size.
requirements.boundary_note: Bowl capacity, depth, and dimensions are attributes of the vessel design; bowl removability is a separate operational behavior.

requirements.title: Quick-Removal and Swappable Bowls
requirements.definition: Each bowl must be easy to lift out, clean, and rapidly exchange during event operation without obstruction from the whisk or motor assembly.
requirements.boundary_note: Bowl removal is independently testable from whisk removal even though the two mechanisms require compatible clearances.

requirements.title: Quick-Release Removable Whisks
requirements.definition: The whisks must detach quickly and straightforwardly, preferably without tools, to permit cleaning, replacement, and bowl removal.
requirements.boundary_note: The release mechanism is separate from the whisk's mixing geometry and can be changed or fail without altering mixing-head selection.

requirements.title: Continuous-Operation Durability
requirements.definition: The machine and its drive system must tolerate prolonged or repeated event operation without overheating, overloading, or mechanical degradation.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers operational duty-cycle endurance; instantaneous speed adjustment, structure stability, and electrical load capacity remain separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Operating Noise Control
requirements.definition: The mixer should avoid excessive operating noise so it remains practical in live-event environments.
requirements.boundary_note: Noise is an independently observable acceptance property and is not merged with structural vibration or mixing quality.

requirements.title: Button-Actuated Controlled Dispensing
requirements.definition: Each station must dispense through a gravity-fed, button-actuated valve system that starts and stops cleanly and produces a smooth, controlled stream without sputtering or continued dripping.
requirements.boundary_note: Solenoid actuation, press-to-dispense behavior, flow rate, and shutoff are attributes of one dispensing mechanism; leakage, cleaning, and spout geometry have separate outcomes.

requirements.title: Spout Geometry and Orientation
requirements.definition: Provide render-like stainless-steel spouts positioned toward the baristas and directing the beverage downward to preserve presentation and drink consistency.
requirements.boundary_note: Physical direction, placement, material, and render-matching form belong to the spout configuration; flow actuation and leak integrity can change independently.

requirements.title: Leak-Free Plumbing
requirements.definition: All bowl outlets, fittings, tubing, valves, and spouts must remain watertight during filling, continuous operation, and dispensing.
requirements.boundary_note: Plumbing integrity has a distinct failure and repair trajectory; controlled flow and electrical isolation must not be treated as the same behavior.

requirements.title: Liquid Isolation from Electrical Components
requirements.definition: The design must prevent beverage or cleaning liquid from seeping into the base or contacting motors, wiring, controllers, and other electrical components.
requirements.boundary_note: Electrical isolation is independently required even if a plumbing leak occurs; it therefore remains separate from the no-leak Requirement.

requirements.title: Cleanable and Removable Dispensing Path
requirements.definition: The spouts and food-contact plumbing must be removable, flushable, or otherwise straightforward to clean between uses without inaccessible residue traps.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers sanitation access for the dispensing path; quick bowl and whisk removal are separate mechanisms with their own event-use purposes.

requirements.title: Raised Cup-Clearance Platform
requirements.definition: Provide a separate support base that raises the mixer enough for standard 12-ounce cups to fit beneath the low-mounted spouts and matches the machine footprint.
requirements.boundary_note: Platform height, cup clearance, and edge-to-edge footprint are attributes of one support mechanism; platform branding is independently changeable.

requirements.title: Standard 120V Wall Power
requirements.definition: The initial prototype must operate from a standard 120V wall outlet using the required internal voltage conversion.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the selected input-power source for V1; a possible future battery adaptation is not treated as a currently required second power mode.

requirements.title: Electrical Load Capacity and Overload Protection
requirements.definition: The power supply and controllers must simultaneously support both motors, solenoids, fans, and controls with sufficient reserve capacity to avoid overload or overheating.
requirements.boundary_note: Power rating and controller capacity form one electrical-load mechanism; the 120V input choice and mechanical duty-cycle durability remain separate.

requirements.title: Functional Master Power Control
requirements.definition: Provide a functional, accessible master switch or button for starting and shutting down the machine without relying on plugging or unplugging it.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers master on/off behavior; the button's lighting and DJ-style appearance belong to visual-design Requirements.

requirements.title: Intuitive Control Panel Layout
requirements.definition: Arrange the station speed controls, dispense controls, and master power control in a simple, accessible, and understandable central interface.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers physical usability and placement of controls, not their underlying speed, dispensing, or power behaviors and not their decorative styling.

requirements.title: Structural Stability and Vibration Control
requirements.definition: The assembled machine must be sturdy and resist rattling, shifting, or excessive tower vibration during operation.
requirements.boundary_note: Base rigidity, feet, and vibration resistance are attributes of structural stability; acoustic noise and splash control have separate acceptance outcomes.

requirements.title: Practical Enclosure Form Factor
requirements.definition: Package the plumbing, motors, controls, and bowls in an enclosure with practical proportions while avoiding unnecessary overall bulk.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers physical dimensions and packaging compromises; color, logos, lighting, and other visual treatments remain separate.

requirements.title: Internal Component Service Access
requirements.definition: Provide removable panels or openings that allow practical maintenance, adjustment, and replacement of motors, electronics, and internal plumbing.
requirements.boundary_note: Service access concerns internal repair and replacement; routine removal of bowls, whisks, and spouts is represented by their specific Requirements.

requirements.title: Food-Safe Contact Materials
requirements.definition: All parts that contact matcha or cleaning liquid must use suitable food-safe materials such as stainless steel and food-grade silicone or plastic.
requirements.boundary_note: Material suitability is independently enforceable from whether a part is removable or easy to sanitize.

requirements.title: Off-the-Shelf Prototype Components
requirements.definition: Use readily available off-the-shelf components where practical to keep the first prototype straightforward, dependable, and economical.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a V1 implementation-strategy constraint rather than a requirement that every component be off-the-shelf; explicitly approved custom parts remain possible.

requirements.title: Beige and Green Color Scheme
requirements.definition: Use the selected beige body treatment with coordinated green accents and matching detail colors.
requirements.boundary_note: Color and finish can be revised independently from logos, lighting, measurement markings, and functional control behavior.

requirements.title: Machine Placard Branding
requirements.definition: Display the specified Matcha Mixer wording on the machine placard with placement and orientation visible to the intended customer and barista viewing directions.
requirements.boundary_note: Wording, placard position, and two-sided visibility form one branding element; branding on the separate support base evolves independently.

requirements.title: Support-Base Logo and Lettering
requirements.definition: Apply coordinated branding to the separate support base using the selected logo treatment, matching font, and all-capital lettering.
requirements.boundary_note: Base branding is physically and semantically independent from the machine's upper placard and from the platform's cup-clearance function.

requirements.title: Bowl Measurement-Ring Markings
requirements.definition: Include measurement-style units or ring markings around the bowls to reinforce the render-inspired DJ appearance.
requirements.boundary_note: The markings are a separately requested visual element and do not define bowl capacity or mixing performance.

requirements.title: Dispense-Button K Markings
requirements.definition: Mark each green dispense button with the selected cursive beige K treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: The K marking has its own wording, color, and implementation trajectory and can be added independently from other decorative controls.

requirements.title: Bowl Accent Lighting
requirements.definition: Add compatible accent lighting in selected locations, including render-inspired lighting around the bowls or power control.
requirements.boundary_note: Lighting is independently selectable, sourceable, and deferrable; it is not merged into a broad aesthetic umbrella.

requirements.title: Power-Button Accent Lighting
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: DJ-Style Decorative Controls
requirements.definition: Use render-inspired DJ details such as silver knobs and buttons, faux controls, Deck 1 and Deck 2 labels, and coordinated back-panel styling.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the coherent DJ-console decorative treatment; operational speed, dispensing, and power-control behavior remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Deck 1 and Deck 2 Labels
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: Back-Panel Design and Font
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

The newest updates look great. Seeing the plumbing, drain routing, bowl integration, and full structure take shape has made me even more enthusiastic about the direction of the project.

Food-contact materials such as stainless steel, food-grade plastics, food-grade silicone, etc.

materials used
CAD files
wiring layout
cleaning procedures
exploded-view drawings if available

We don’t need all of that immediately, but if this develops into a larger project, that information could be extremely valuable. Everything looks fantastic overall, and I’m very excited to see the testing videos and completed assembly. It’s incredible to watch this go from an idea to a real machine.

source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001] — I reviewed the BOM, and I really like the overall direction. It matches what I was hoping for.

Before we proceed, I’d like your thoughts on a few items:

• Motors — I’m concerned that 200 RPM could be slightly too slow to produce a strong, frothy matcha texture. Would increasing the RPM make sense while still preserving enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — compared with the resin whisk, would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head provide better consistency, durability, and foam quality?

• Spout — I want to continue with the solenoid solution. The pour needs to be clean, controlled, and seamless (mix → open → pour), both to protect the texture and create the right visual experience.

• Splash / mess control — this matters a lot for events. I want to ensure:
– little to no splashing while mixing
– a smooth, controlled stream from the spout without sputtering
– no drips after the valve closes
– effective seals so nothing leaks into the base
– a splash guard or lip around the bowl if one is necessary

• Cleaning — if possible, the bowls and spout parts should either be removable or otherwise easy to clean.

I’m happy with everything else. I’d like to know what you think about these points and whether you would change anything before we finalize the BOM.

Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

The newest updates look great. Seeing the plumbing, drain routing, bowl integration, and full structure take shape has made me even more enthusiastic about the direction of the project.

While thinking about the future, I keep considering the possibility of eventually placing the Matcha Mixer in a retail setting if we decide to open a shop. For that reason, I’d like us to begin considering food-service and health department requirements now, while the machine is still at the prototype stage.

As development continues, I’d like to keep the following points in mind:

Food-contact materials such as stainless steel, food-grade plastics, food-grade silicone, etc.
Ease of sanitation and cleaning
Avoiding concealed spaces where liquid could collect or become trapped
Simple removal of the bowls, whisks, and other parts for cleaning
Keeping liquids separated from electrical components
Access for maintenance and servicing if a component ever requires replacement

When you have time, I’d also like to learn which materials are used wherever food contact occurs and whether you anticipate any areas presenting cleaning or sanitation difficulties.

Over the long term, I think retaining documentation for the following would be useful:

materials used
CAD files
wiring layout
cleaning procedures
exploded-view drawings if available

We don’t need all of that immediately, but if this develops into a larger project, that information could be extremely valuable. Everything looks fantastic overall, and I’m very excited to see the testing videos and completed assembly. It’s incredible to watch this go from an idea to a real machine.

[CLIENT_NAME_001] Burton

source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I fully understand your frustration with the uncertain timeline and your need to manage your business schedule urgently. I’m sorry that I was unavailable over the weekend. To provide an accurate delivery schedule today, I needed to carefully go back through our design history.

For clarity on the build’s current status, the short video I sent on June 6th showed only an internal engineering test of the raw, disassembled plumbing. Its purpose was to confirm that the core mechanics function flawlessly; it was not intended to present a completed housing.

During our June 7th discussion about aesthetic upgrades, I explained that adding embedded custom text, measurement rings, dual-sided logos, and LED lighting would mean completely scrapping the physical chassis I had already built according to the initially approved specifications. Making extensive visual modifications before testing the internal mechanics under load is highly risky. We could finish an attractive shell, discover that a mechanical component must be changed, and then be forced to discard the physical base again.

To protect your investment and remove the uncertainty, we need to select one of these two approaches today:

Option 1 (Prioritize Functionality & Delivery): We retain the currently approved design scope, allowing me to perform the core engineering tests this week. The fully operational V1 prototype will be ready to ship by Friday or Monday. The complete cosmetic redesign, including LEDs, silver DJ knobs, and logos, can then be completed later through a separate V2 milestone contract.

Option 2 (Execute the Aesthetic Overhaul Now): If you would rather stop the mechanical deployment and immediately reproduce all of the rendering’s visual details, production must be formally rolled back. A separate, new milestone on Upwork will be required to pay for the additional re-engineering time, sourcing of new components, and the cost of the discarded physical materials.
